In an in-depth interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and discussed future plans for a tab-less interface. The full interview can be viewed below.

In the future, work may be seamlessly completed within ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern first released a preview clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Today, Stern released the full interview, covering the new ChatGPT Voice, OpenAI's hardware development plans, the lawsuit with Apple, and the recent breach at Hugging Face.

During the interview, Stern mentioned OpenAI's earlier decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps, along with the launch of the new agent mode, Work.

The merged interface left users quite confused, especially those who just wanted to continue using ChatGPT but struggled to find their conversation history.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top of the interface, and a dropdown menu in the left sidebar to switch between ChatGPT and Codex. Although it is no longer as difficult as before, the interface remains somewhat cumbersome.

Asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern's description of the new interface as "a bit of a mess" and added that this is a "stepping stone" toward the future, where the Work tab will disappear and its functionality will "seamlessly integrate into ChatGPT".

Brockman also said that despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI has seen the expected results, with Codex users surging from 5 million to 10 million in just a few days.

When pressed on whether the growth was purely due to "cramming" Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman acknowledged it again, but argued that to some extent, this was part of the plan:

The entire interview is excellent and definitely worth watching. It also includes a very Joanna Stern-style attempt to bring ChatGPT Voice into the conversation—and the result is exactly as you would imagine.
